_: Conversational test lines in the app's own style (written for this project, free to use). Only for final checks, never tuned on.

lines.text: Hi there! I'm so glad you stopped by.
Oh, hello. I wasn't expecting anyone today.
Well, well, look who finally decided to show up.
Hmm, let me think about that for a moment.
Honestly? I have no idea what you mean.
Wait, did you just say what I think you said?
No, no, no. That's not how it works at all.
My mum makes the best pumpkin bread in the whole town.
I've never felt so alive in my entire life!
Who knew you'd come through for us in the end?
You know what? Maybe you're right. Maybe I'm wrong.
Let's grab a coffee and talk it over, shall we?
I was born in a tiny village by the sea, a long, long time ago.
People say I'm stubborn. I prefer the word determined.
Please, call me Bob. Everybody does.
It's quarter past nine, and I've already had three cups of tea.
We should probably get moving before it starts to rain.
Oh boy. This is going to be a very long week.
Do you remember the first time we met? You looked terrified.
That's brilliant! Why didn't I think of that?
I'm not angry. I'm just a little bit disappointed.
Every morning I walk my dog, Pepper, along the river.
Fine. Have it your way. But don't come crying to me later.
Ah, the smell of fresh bread. Nothing beats it.
I could tell you, but then I'd have to make you promise to keep it secret.
Mm, maybe tomorrow. Today I'm just too tired.
Look, I don't want any trouble. I'm only passing through.
Thank you, really. That means more to me than you know.
Seventy-two days at sea, and not a single storm. Can you believe it?
Shh! Keep your voice down, they might hear us.
What a wonderful surprise! Come in, come in.
I've been thinking about moving somewhere warm. Maybe Portugal, maybe Mexico.
Some people collect stamps. I collect stories.
Are you sure about this? Because once we start, there's no going back.
My brother Paul borrowed my bike and broke the back wheel.
Wow. Just, wow. I'm speechless.
The meeting is on Monday at ten, in the big room upstairs.
If you ever need a hand, you know where to find me.
I used to be a baker, before all of this happened.
Please don't touch that. It's very old, and very fragile.
Oh, you're good. You're really, really good.
Remember: measure twice, cut once.
I'm hungry. Are you hungry? Let's find some food.
Maybe the problem isn't the map. Maybe it's the people reading it.
Back in my day, we walked five miles to school, both ways.
Well, that went better than expected. Mostly.
Ha! I knew it. I knew you'd say that.
My favourite movie? Probably something with pirates and a big, booming soundtrack.
Hold on, I'm almost finished. Just one more minute.
I promise I'll be back before midnight. Probably.
Could you pass me the pepper and the butter, please?
Twenty-three, forty-seven, ninety-nine. Those were the winning numbers.
Ugh, Mondays. Why do they always feel so long?
Be brave. Be bold. And maybe bring a jumper.
Wonderful weather we're having, isn't it? Perfect for a picnic.
I've made up my mind. We're moving to the mountains in May.
Mmm, this soup is amazing. What's in it?
Please, please, please tell me you brought the map.
Bye for now. Be safe, and say hello to your mother for me.
Good morning! Did you sleep well? You look much better today.
